original.target_description: Unassigned original side; placeholder only. Original primary source is outside this source-group assignment.

replication.target_description: Primary random-effects meta-analysis of 19 labs: Ten Commandments-cheat versus books-cheat conditions, self-reported number of matrices solved. Identified by moral-prime manipulation, primary-analysis description on printed p. 304 (article p. 6), and Fig. 2 on printed p. 306.

n.sample_role: Participants in the two mutually exclusive final cheat conditions contributing to the primary meta-analysis across 19 laboratories; 19 labs are the meta-analytic units.
n.exclusions: Excludes both control conditions. Source inclusion criteria: 18–25-year-old students, sample 20%–80% female, followed instructions and completed necessary tasks; exclusions for incorrect administration, sessions under 50, failure to tear out page, reporting over 20 matrices, or listing no books/Commandments and spending no recall time. Primary sample allows documented data-blind exceptions; 4,674 is the larger four-condition primary sample, not the target contrast N.
n.location: Printed p. 306, Fig. 2, Meta-Analytic Average row; p. 304, Inclusion criteria and Primary analyses.

es.metric: mean difference in matrices (Commandments-cheat minus books-cheat)
es.location: Printed p. 304 (article p. 6), Primary analyses; printed p. 306, Fig. 2.
es.quote: participants reported solving 0.11 more matrices in the ... Commandments-cheat condition than in the books- ... cheat condition (95% confidence interval, CI = [−0.09, ... 0.31]; Fig. 2).

reported_success.quote: In sum, we did not observe the predicted reduction ... in cheating following priming with the Ten Command- ... ments. These results call into question the effectiveness ... of using the Ten Commandments as a moral prime to ... reduce cheating.

notes: Identity independently verified from title Registered Replication Report on Mazar, Amir, and Ariely (2008), Bruno Verschuere et al. author list, DOI 10.1177/2515245918781032, journal 2018 volume 1(3), pp. 299–317, and explicit direct-replication description. Candidate is full primary report text including Results, figures, Discussion and references, not a preregistration or secondary excerpt. No PDF path supplied; no PDF rendering performed. Target identified by manipulation/outcome/primary comparison and locator, independently of row order or numeric matching. Analytic participant N derived solely from explicit final, mutually exclusive Fig. 2 group totals: 1,100 Commandments-cheat + 1,194 books-cheat = 2,294. The 4,674 primary-analysis participants include control conditions and are not used for this contrast. Mean difference 0.11 is retained as printed; its CI is [−0.09, 0.31], and printed Cohen’s d is −0.04 (95% CI [−0.12, 0.04]). Neither is converted. No test statistic or p for the primary mean difference is printed in its Results paragraph/Fig. 2. Q(18) = 13.16, p = .78 tests heterogeneity; slope 0.17, p = .20 tests religiousness moderation, and neither is the requested primary comparison. For audit 1936, requested test-statistic metric is not printed for this contrast; the available printed mean difference is retained with explicit metric. Both assigned descriptions locate this same primary moral-priming contrast.
